heading.text: The molecule behind the lift: caffeine

presence.note: Made by the coffee plant; it carries into the brewed cup.

text.text: The molecule behind coffee's lift: it keeps you feeling alert by getting in the way of your brain's own sleepiness signal.

more.text: Caffeine works by impersonation: it fits the brain's receptors for adenosine, the sleepiness signal that builds up the longer you are awake, without switching them on.
Coffee, tea and cocoa plants each evolved their own way of making it, and in the leaves it is a natural pesticide.

heading.text: How it works: caffeine blocks adenosine

presence.note: Your body makes it; caffeine blocks its receptors.

text.text: The 'time to rest' signal that slowly builds up while you are awake; caffeine works by blocking it.

more.text: Adenosine is a molecule your body makes continuously while you are awake, and as it accumulates and settles onto its receptors, you feel more and more like sleeping.

ref.starts: Adenosine is a molecule your body makes

more.text: Caffeine happens to fit those same receptors closely enough to occupy them without switching them on, so the sleepiness signal keeps being sent and stops being heard.
When the caffeine clears, the adenosine that piled up in the meantime is still there and lands all at once, which is what an afternoon crash actually is.

presence.note: Your liver makes it from caffeine.

heading.text: What caffeine becomes: paraxanthine

text.text: The main thing caffeine turns into inside you, and much of what actually keeps you feeling awake after a cup.

requires: the referenced line says 'caffeine blocks its receptors'
the referenced line says 'caffeine turns into'

heading.text: A gentler cousin in chocolate: theobromine

presence.note: From the cocoa bean.

text.text: Chocolate's gentle stimulant, a milder cousin of caffeine that gives cocoa its lingering lift and faint bitterness.

number.text: about 150 to 250 mg per serving of dark chocolate

more.text: That one group changes how strongly each binds the brain's adenosine receptors, and caffeine binds far harder, which is why coffee arrives as a jolt and chocolate does not.
Theobromine lingers longer instead, with a half-life around 7.2 hours against caffeine's 5, so cocoa's lift is slower and flatter.
Both come from the same plants in different proportions: coffee and tea lead with caffeine, cocoa leads with theobromine.

ref.starts: Both come from the same plants

page_title.text: What's in the medicine cabinet: Tylenol, Advil, NyQuil, Vicks

description.text: The active ingredients on Tylenol, Advil, NyQuil and Vicks VapoRub, as each label states them, and how acetaminophen, ibuprofen and menthol work.

lede.text: Read the labels on Tylenol, Advil, NyQuil and Vicks VapoRub, and meet the molecule behind each active ingredient they list, with the strength each label states.

heading.text: The pain reliever Tylenol and NyQuil share: acetaminophen

text.text: The pain and fever reliever sold as Tylenol and Panadol, called paracetamol outside the US. More than a century after it was first made, how it eases pain is still not fully understood.

more.text: Acetaminophen, sold as Tylenol or paracetamol, eases pain and fever without the stomach irritation of the NSAIDs.

Acetaminophen, called paracetamol outside the US, acts mainly in the central nervous system and does very little for inflammation, which is why a sprain and a headache are not the same problem for it.

heading.text: Advil's ibuprofen, which eases inflammation too

text.text: The anti-inflammatory painkiller sold as Advil and Motrin. It is sold as a mirror-image pair, and the body turns much of the inactive form into the active one.

more.text: Ibuprofen is an NSAID: it blocks the COX enzymes throughout the body, which is why it reduces inflammation and swelling as well as pain.
Ibuprofen is the everyday anti-inflammatory, blocking the COX enzymes that build the prostaglandins behind pain, fever, and swelling.

heading.text: The cool and the warm in Vicks VapoRub: menthol and camphor

text.text: The cold feeling of peppermint, chewing gum, and cough drops. It does not lower the temperature, it opens the same nerve channel that real cold does.
The penetrating smell of Vicks VapoRub and mothballs, tapped from the camphor laurel tree and now mostly made from turpentine.

more.text: Menthol activates TRPM8, the cold receptor, which is why it feels cool without lowering any temperature, and it is the reason peppermint and menthol cigarettes feel the way they do.

Camphor is less selective, working on several TRP channels including the warm ones, which is why it reads as both cooling and warming and why it appears in chest rubs alongside menthol rather than instead of it.

text.text: A longer-acting anti-inflammatory painkiller sold as Aleve, used for pain, fever, and inflammation.

line.text: Starch, the glucose chain you digest, and cellulose, the one you cannot.

lede.text: Start with starch, the glucose chain your body takes apart, then meet cellulose, the same glucose joined by a bond your enzymes cannot cut, and maltodextrin, starch cut short. End at the crust, where baking makes the smell.

heading.text: The glucose chain you digest: starch

presence.note: From the flour.

text.text: How plants store glucose, and the biggest single source of calories in the human diet. Bread, rice, potatoes, and pasta are largely this.

more.text: Neither contains anything but glucose.
Starch links its glucose units with alpha bonds, which human amylase can cut, so starch is food.

heading.text: The same glucose, a bond you cannot digest: cellulose

presence_absent.text: Not on our bread list: cellulose is here as starch's counterpart, the same glucose joined the other way.

text.text: The most abundant organic polymer on earth: long chains of glucose that build every plant cell wall. Cotton is nearly pure cellulose.

more.text: Cellulose links them with beta bonds, which flips every second unit over and produces a flat ribbon that human enzymes cannot touch, so cellulose is dietary fibre.

ref.starts: Cellulose links them with beta bonds

more.text: Those flat ribbons stack and hydrogen-bond into fibres, which is why cellulose is structural in plants and starch is not: one is the plant's warehouse and the other is its scaffolding.
Cows and termites manage cellulose only by hosting microbes that carry the missing enzyme.

heading.text: Starch cut short: maltodextrin

presence_absent.text: Not on our bread list: maltodextrin is made from starch, and it is here to show what starch becomes when its chains are cut.

text.text: A short chain of glucose units cut from starch by acid or enzymes. It bulks up powders and thickens sauces, and it tastes barely sweet.

more.text: Maltodextrin is the same glucose chains cut down to a few units, which makes it dissolve instantly, taste faintly sweet where starch tastes of nothing, and raise blood glucose faster than table sugar does.

ref.starts: Maltodextrin is the same glucose chains

more.text: Starch is the storage form plants actually make; maltodextrin is an industrial product.

page_title.text: What's in sugar and sweeteners: sucrose to sucralose

description.text: Sucrose sets the sweetness scale at 1. Aspartame, sucralose and stevioside are hundreds of times sweeter; xylitol and erythritol are one carbon apart.

lede.text: Sucrose, table sugar, sets the sweetness scale at 1. Follow it to aspartame, sucralose and stevioside, each hundreds of times sweeter, and to xylitol and erythritol, two sugar alcohols one carbon apart.

requires: aspartame is at least 100 × sugar

heading.text: The yardstick: sucrose, table sugar

presence.note: Table sugar is sucrose, refined from sugar cane or sugar beet.

text.text: Table sugar: one glucose joined to one fructose. It is the reference point the whole sweetness scale is measured against, at exactly 1 times sweet.

more.text: Sucrose, ordinary table sugar, is the yardstick every other sweetener is measured against.
By definition it sits at 1x on the sweetness scale; a sweetener rated "200x" simply tastes as sweet at one two-hundredth the amount.
The bond joining sucrose's two halves is split by the enzyme sucrase in the small intestine.

ref.starts: The bond joining sucrose's two halves

heading.text: Two hundred times sweeter: aspartame

presence.note: The sweetener the maker adds.

text.text: The sweetener in blue packets, diet sodas and sugar-free gum, about 200 times sweeter than sugar. It is a dipeptide, so it carries a phenylalanine warning label.

more.text: Aspartame is roughly two hundred times sweeter than sugar, so a diet soda needs only a trace of it to match the sweetness of the ~40 grams of sugar in a regular can, with almost none of the calories.

ref.starts: Aspartame is roughly two hundred times

more.text: Aspartame is not a carbohydrate at all but a dipeptide, phenylalanine joined to aspartic acid, which the body does break down, and that is why products carry a phenylalanine warning for people with phenylketonuria.

ref.starts: Aspartame is not a carbohydrate at all

requires: the referenced line says 'about 200 times sweeter than sugar'
the Soft drinks list carries aspartame

heading.text: Sugar with three chlorines: sucralose

presence.note: The sweetener the maker adds.

text.text: The sweetener in yellow packets, sold as Splenda. It is table sugar with three chlorine atoms swapped in, which makes it 600 times sweeter and indigestible.

more.text: Sucralose is roughly six hundred times sweeter than sugar, built by swapping three of sucrose's hydroxyl groups for chlorine.

ref.starts: Sucralose is roughly six hundred times

more.text: Sucralose actually starts as sucrose with three hydroxyl groups swapped for chlorine, which is why its formula carries Cl3 and why the body cannot digest it: the enzymes no longer recognise the shape.
Sucralose is chlorinated sucrose that the body cannot digest and that survives baking, while aspartame is a dipeptide the body breaks down and heat destroys.

requires: the referenced line says 'three chlorine atoms'
C12H19Cl3O8 minus C12H22O11 is Cl3H-3O-3

heading.text: From a leaf: stevioside

presence.note: Made in the leaves of the stevia plant.

text.text: The most abundant sweet compound in stevia leaves, around 300 times sweeter than sugar but with a liquorice bitterness that rebaudioside A lacks.

more.text: Stevioside is the sweet molecule extracted from the leaves of the stevia plant, about three hundred times sweeter than sugar.
Because it comes from a leaf rather than a lab, it anchors the natural end of the high-intensity sweeteners.

ref.starts: Because it comes from a leaf

more.text: Sucralose is made in a factory from sugar and stevioside is extracted from the stevia leaf, and sucralose is the sweeter of the two.
Stevioside and rebaudioside A are steviol glycosides from the same leaf, one sugar unit apart, and rebaudioside A lacks stevioside's liquorice bitterness.

heading.text: One carbon apart: xylitol and erythritol

presence.note: The sweetener the maker adds.

text.text: The sugar alcohol in sugar-free gum, as sweet as sugar but not fermentable by mouth bacteria, which is why dentists like it. It is toxic to dogs.

presence.note: The sweetener the maker adds.

text.text: A sugar alcohol about 60 percent as sweet as sugar that the body absorbs and excretes largely unchanged, which is why it carries almost no calories.

more.text: Xylitol and erythritol are sugar alcohols one carbon apart; xylitol is about as sweet as sugar and toxic to dogs, while erythritol is less sweet and is not.

Erythritol is absorbed in the small intestine and excreted largely unchanged, so it reaches the gut bacteria in small amounts and causes less digestive upset; xylitol is fermented further along and is the more likely of the two to cause it.

ref.starts: Erythritol is absorbed in the small intestine

requires: C5H12O5 minus C4H10O4 is CH2O

page_title.text: What's in household cleaners: ammonia, bleach, peroxide, sodas

description.text: What ammonia, bleach and hydrogen peroxide each do when they clean, and how baking soda, washing soda and caustic soda differ in how strongly alkaline each is.

lede.text: Follow ammonia, bleach and hydrogen peroxide to what each one does when it cleans, then meet three sodas, from the baking soda that lifts a cake to the caustic soda in drain cleaner.

heading.text: For glass and grease: ammonia

presence.note: The maker adds it to glass and grease cleaners.

text.text: The sharp, eye-watering smell of window cleaner and cat litter. Made from the nitrogen in air by the Haber-Bosch process, it is where synthetic fertilizer begins.

more.text: Ammonia is the far smaller molecule at 17.03 against 74.44 and is a gas dissolved in water rather than a salt.

ref.starts: Ammonia is the far smaller molecule

requires: the referenced line says 'Ammonia cleans glass and grease'

heading.text: What bleach is: sodium hypochlorite

presence.note: The active ingredient of chlorine bleach.

text.text: Household bleach. In water it releases hypochlorous acid, which destroys the pigments in a stain and the proteins in a microbe.

more.text: Sodium hypochlorite releases hypochlorous acid in water, which is the active destroyer of stain pigments and microbial proteins, and it leaves salt behind.
Ammonia cleans glass and grease and sodium hypochlorite is bleach, and mixing the two makes chloramines, a toxic gas that badly irritates the airways.

heading.text: Water and oxygen, nothing else: hydrogen peroxide

presence.note: The active ingredient of oxygen bleach.

text.text: The pale blue liquid sold as a 3 percent solution for cleaning cuts and bleaching hair. It breaks down into water and oxygen, which is the fizzing.

more.text: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen and nothing else, which is why it is the one used on fabric and hair where a chlorine smell would be unwelcome.
Hydrogen peroxide breaks down into only water and oxygen, while sodium hypochlorite, household bleach, leaves salt behind and is the stronger disinfectant.

heading.text: Three sodas: baking, washing and caustic

presence.note: Sold as baking soda, and added to cleaners.

text.text: Baking soda. It releases carbon dioxide when it meets an acid, which is why it lifts a cake and why it fizzes in a glass of vinegar.

presence.note: Sold as washing soda, and added to detergents.

text.text: Washing soda: the water softener in laundry powder, the flux that lets glass melt at a workable temperature, and a common pH raiser for pools.

presence.note: The active ingredient of drain and oven cleaners.

text.text: Lye, the caustic base of drain cleaner and oven cleaner, and the thing that turns fat into soap. It is corrosive to skin on contact.

more.text: Baking soda and washing soda are the same two elements in different proportions, NaHCO3 against Na2CO3, and the extra sodium makes all the difference to how alkaline they are.

ref.starts: Baking soda and washing soda are the same two elements

more.text: Heating baking soda in an oven converts it into washing soda, releasing carbon dioxide and water, which is the same reaction that raises a cake.

ref.starts: Heating baking soda in an oven

more.text: In baking, the carbon dioxide is the point; in cleaning, the alkalinity is.

ref.starts: In baking, the carbon dioxide is the point

more.text: Sodium hydroxide is caustic soda, strong enough to saponify fat and dissolve hair, which is what makes it the active ingredient in drain cleaner and in soap making.

requires: the referenced line says 'opposite ends of that scale'

text.text: EDTA, the molecule that grabs metal ions and will not let go. It keeps mayonnaise from going rancid, stops blood samples clotting, and is the antidote in lead poisoning.

heading.text: A vitamin your body cannot make: vitamin C

presence.note: Made by the fruit.

text.text: Vitamin C, the tart brightness of citrus and a nutrient your body cannot make on its own.

more.text: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, which humans cannot make and must eat; citric acid is not a vitamin at all and the body produces it constantly as part of the citric acid cycle.

heading.text: Sour, and not a vitamin at all: citric acid

presence.note: The main acid of citrus juice.

text.text: The mouth-watering sourness of lemons, limes, and oranges.

more.text: Citric acid preserves by lowering pH, while ascorbic acid preserves by being oxidised in place of the food, which is why it stops cut apples browning.

ref.starts: Citric acid preserves by lowering pH

more.text: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, a vitamin humans must get from food, while citric acid is not a vitamin at all and the body makes it constantly.
Acetic acid has one acid group and is the sour and smell of vinegar, while citric acid has three, is an odourless solid and binds metal ions well.
